gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-nandin: Fuzzy Bubbles draws round, friendly letters with a line that never swells or thins, like a drafting pen. And Noto Sans Nandinagari follows in a plain sans with generous openings and short ascenders, so the two sit together easily.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-newa: Hand-lettered and loose, Fuzzy Bubbles runs on a rope-thin outline with no thick or thin parts, and small letters nearly as tall as its capitals. Noto Sans Newa then reads with open, tall-bodied lowercase.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Neon-tube strokes, soft and round: that is Fuzzy Bubbles, relaxed and personal in every letter it draws. And Noto Sans Nushu stands tall beneath it, a sans with a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Relaxed is the first thing Fuzzy Bubbles says, in rounded handwritten letters. Noto Sans Ogham brings wide gaps in the e and tall lowercase bodies that look bold, a sans-serif sturdiness set against the heading's drafting-pen line.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-ol-chi: Fuzzy Bubbles looks like bent wire, a handwritten line of constant thickness with rounded, open letters. Noto Sans Ol Chiki sits next to it more tidily, curve tails held well back, words forming solid blocks that make the heading look looser.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-old-hu: Approachable from the first glance, Noto Sans Old Hungarian offers tall a, e and s shapes whose big openings stay clear at tiny sizes. Fuzzy Bubbles adds its rolling-ball pen trail above.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-old-it: Noto Sans Old Italic is a sans with almost no gap between x-height and cap height, and its curve endings stay well apart. But Fuzzy Bubbles above it is handwritten, with thin joins no thinner than the stems, so the two look related yet loose.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-old-no: Noto Sans Old North Arabian forms a dense, tall lowercase band, its terminals pointing outward like a pair of tongs. Under Fuzzy Bubbles, whose stroke ends look cut from one ribbon, a long read feels friendly and steady.
gen-gf-fuzzy-bubbles-gf-noto-sans-old-pe: Noto Sans Old Permic reads as rounded and open to the side, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals in height. Over a long page that plain sans stays friendly, while Fuzzy Bubbles keeps its tube-like thickness through every bend.

Relaxed and personal, Fuzzy Bubbles writes with no thick-and-thin contrast to slow the eye, in round handwritten shapes. Noto Sans Old Persian adds lofty lowercase and open counters, a sans-serif body that gives the heading plenty of space.
